origin: Researcher-designed, 2026-09-23, directly implementing a published academic finding rather than an internally-invented technical pattern -- see dates.md for citations (Gao/Han/Li/Zhou 2018 JFE; Baltussen/van Vliet/Ye 2021).
timeframe: M1 (tick-driven for the window-boundary price captures; timeframe is otherwise cosmetic)
thesis: The London session's first half-hour return predicts its last half-hour return in the same direction -- a documented, peer-reviewed, cross-asset-class (including currencies) intraday momentum effect, not an internally-invented technical pattern.
broker_clock_conversion: 08:00 London = 10:00 server, 16:00 London = 18:00 server, constant year-round.

entry.measurement: first_move_pips = price at 10:30 server - price at 10:00 server (sign only, no magnitude filter in v1 -- stays faithful to the literature's construction)
entry.trigger: at 17:30 server (start of the last half-hour), enter in the direction of first_move_pips's sign
skip_conditions: computed lot size below broker minimum (never rounded up)
MinFirstMovePips filter if set > 0 (off by default)

stop_loss: fixed 20 pips (day-trading scale, matches gotobi's convention -- the research studies return predictability, not a specific stop-loss discipline, so this is this project's own risk-management choice)
take_profit: none -- closed by the clock at session end (18:00 server), same convention as gotobi/wm_fix_reversal

exit.rule: market close at session end (18:00 server) if SL not hit first

tunable_parameters_to_sweep: StopLossPips, MinFirstMovePips (currently 0/off, faithful to the literature) -- not yet swept, v1 tests the pure literature-faithful construction first before any tuning.

demo_criteria.rationale: Standard day_trading category anchor -- one trade per trading day expected, similar cadence to gotobi/wm_fix_reversal.
